Monthly shift swaps rules
New handlers should know how a new handler works

This page matters because the desk runs on steady judgment, clear handoffs, and calm communication. When a traveler brings in an animal, your job is to keep the process humane, orderly, and easy to follow. At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk is where routine service becomes safe service, so every interaction has to feel confident and warm.

Start by listening closely and speaking in a friendly, professional tone. New staff should welcome questions without sounding rushed, because nervous travelers pick up on your pace right away. Keep your notes simple and exact, and pass anything unusual to the senior coordinator before you promise an answer. Never guess when an animal seems unsettled or a document looks incomplete. Calm handling is not a slogan here; it is the standard.

Treat every carrier as if it needs careful attention from the first touch. If the animal is stressed, lower your voice, reduce movement, and give the ground team enough room to move the carrier safely between services. Do not crowd the area or try to hurry a transfer. Small, steady actions keep the work humane and prevent avoidable mistakes.

When a traveler asks for help, stay present and direct. Use plain language, check the details that matter, and keep the conversation focused on what can be done next. The desk should feel organized even on a busy day, and that depends on you staying calm when others are not. If you do not know something, say so at once and bring in the senior coordinator.

Remember that careful words, careful hands, and careful handoffs protect both the traveler and the animal.
